content:
The test image shows a soybean seedling with a brown lesion on the stem/hypocotyl near the soil line. Key features:
- Firm-looking, brown/dark dry lesion at or near the soil line
- Stem otherwise green and healthy-looking above and below
- No water-soaked appearance
- Hairy stem surface (normal soybean trichomes)

Top candidates: **Rhizoctonia** (reddish-brown, sunken, firm/dry canker at soil line), Pythium (water-soaked, softer), Phytophthora (chocolate-brown discoloration extending up stem).

The Rhizoctonia reference (bottom-left) shows a very similar reddish-brown lesion on a young stem near the soil - matching what I see in the test image. Phytophthora shows more extensive stem discoloration extending up multiple nodes. Pythium shows water-soaked rotting at a very early seedling stage.

**Initial prediction: Rhizoctonia** - The test image shows a young soybean seedling with a firm, dry, brown/reddish-brown lesion on the hypocotyl at or near the soil line, which is the classic presentation.

Now reading the Attractor Guide:

Rhizoctonia is **not listed** as an over-predicted class. Interestingly, the guide notes Phytophthora is over-predicted with Rhizoctonia being the actual class 3x — this further supports my prediction.

**Confirming Rhizoctonia:**
- Young seedling with a firm, dry, reddish-brown lesion/canker on the hypocotyl at the soil line
- Stem remains green above the lesion (no extensive upward discoloration as in Phytophthora)
- No water-soaked/soft rot appearance (rules out Pythium)
- Matches the Rhizoctonia reference closely (bottom-left quadrant showed an identical reddish-brown canker on a stem held near soil)
